I farm 200 mu with just two people in the household, so I will keep the plan simple and labor-efficient. I have 25 years of experience, and in Quzhou County my main backbone will still be the wheat-maize rotation because it matches my land, my irrigation conditions, and what I know best. I will put most of the land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that gives me the most stable use of the land across the full year. I will keep a smaller area in millet because it is hardy and does not need as much water or management. I will also keep some cabbage, but not too much, because cabbage needs more hands, more pest control, and closer field management. Since I have well irrigation, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, keep fertilizer at moderate-to-strong levels on wheat, maize, and cabbage, and stay more moderate on millet. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and easier for my household labor to manage. My goal is steady output, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield on every mu.
